summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with suprapubic pain consistent with a recurrent urinary tract infection, given his history of a chronic indwelling Foley catheter and prior multidrug-resistant UTIs. He was started empirically on ciprofloxacin, which was confirmed appropriate when urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae sensitive to ciprofloxacin. His pain improved over the hospital stay, and he completed three days of a seven-day antibiotic course at discharge. He experienced a brief episode of chest pain radiating to the jaw, but cardiac workup was reassuring with no enzymatic or EKG changes. His anxiety and depression were ongoing concerns; he expressed social withdrawal and fear of being alone, and was maintained on citalopram and duloxetine. Constipation was managed with an aggressive bowel regimen including lactulose. He was discharged to a rehab facility with plans for outpatient follow-up regarding antibiotic suppressive therapy, continuation of ciprofloxacin, and monitoring of mood, mobility, and bowel function.
